idiom_name: toMessage/fromMessage module functions over plain-object messages; JSON.stringify at the endpoint
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no mapper-class culture: the message is a plain object, the mapper is a module exporting pure toMessage(order) and fromMessage(message) functions, and the endpoint owns the encoding (JSON.stringify/JSON.parse or the client library's serialiser). Because plain objects carry no types, the mapper functions are the contract: keep them in one module that imports the domain and is imported by neither shape's owner, and avoid a toJSON() method on the domain class unless the message really is a field-for-field projection - it puts the wire shape into the model and hides the mapping from review.
pitfalls: JSON.stringify drops undefined fields and functions while toJSON() on a nested object can leak internals: decide the absent policy in the mapper instead of relying on the encoder.
JSON.parse returns prototype-less objects, so a fromMessage that calls methods on the payload breaks; construct domain values explicitly.
Dates and big integers lose type and precision through JSON (Date becomes a string, ids beyond 2^53 round): state units and formats in the mapper.
Object spread copies only own enumerable properties and silently drops class getters, which is exactly how a mapped field goes missing without an error.
